chunks: 3304 - And it was narrated from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Establish testimony against the parents and the child, but do not establish it against a brother in religion out of harm.”

I said: What is harm? He said: “It is when the person entitled to the right transgresses regarding it, in what he claims against him, contrary to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله have commanded. An example of that is when one man has a debt against another while he is in hardship, and Allah, the Exalted, has commanded granting him respite until he becomes able, so He said:
And he asks you to establish testimony while you know his hardship, so it is not permissible for you to establish the testimony in the state of hardship.”

key_terms.الشَّهَادَةَ: testimony or witness-bearing in a legal context
key_terms.الضَّيْرُ: harm or injurious consequence caused through testimony
key_terms.الْأَخِ فِي الدِّينِ: a brother in religion, meaning a fellow believer
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a debt owed by one person to another
key_terms.مَيْسَرَةٍ: ease or the point at which the debtor becomes able to pay
key_terms.مُعْسِرٌ: one in financial hardship or insolvency

ai.seo_question: When is it not permissible to give testimony against a debtor in Islam?
ai.summary: The hadith teaches that testimony should be established with justice, even regarding parents and children, but not in a way that causes wrongful harm to a believing brother. It explains that harm occurs when a claimant demands enforcement of a right in a manner contrary to the command of Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, such as pressing a debt claim against someone known to be in hardship.
